risk_factors.heading: We are sensitive to the effects of our major customers’ labor relations.
risk_factors.quote: we are affected by labor difficulties and work stoppages at OEMs’ facilities, such as the UAW strikes that occurred in 2023.

risk_factors.heading: We could be adversely affected by supply shortages of components from our suppliers.
risk_factors.quote: we remain dependent on fewer sources of supply for certain components used in the manufacture of our products.

risk_factors.heading: Suppliers’ economic distress could result in supply interruptions and, in turn, disrupt our operations and adversely affect our business.
risk_factors.quote: In certain instances, it would be difficult and expensive for us to change suppliers that are critical to our business.

risk_factors.heading: We are subject to possible insolvency of financial counterparties.
risk_factors.quote: We are subject to the risk that one or more of these counterparties may become insolvent and, therefore, be unable to meet its obligations under such contracts.

risk_factors.heading: The spin-off of PHINIA may not achieve anticipated tax benefits and may expose us to additional tax risks.
risk_factors.quote: If the spin-off is ultimately determined to be taxable, the Company, PHINIA, or the Company’s stockholders could incur income tax liabilities that could be significant.

risk_factors.heading: Potential liabilities pursuant to the spin-off of PHINIA could materially and adversely affect our business.
risk_factors.quote: If we are required to indemnify PHINIA and other parties under the circumstances set forth in the agreements with PHINIA, we may be subject to future liabilities.

risk_factors.heading: A variety of other factors could adversely affect our business.
risk_factors.quote: the loss of or changes in supply contracts or sourcing strategies of our major customers or suppliers; start-up expenses associated with new vehicle programs or delays or cancellation of such programs
